_comment: Fit curve to data (Qt: ui/curve_fit_dialog.py). The curve's parameters, and nDXplorer's constants the equations read; a freed constant moves the data.

sections.label: Fit to:
sections.description: The displayed data fits y(x) to the two-dimensional distribution (one point per populated x column); a marginal fits the curve to that axis's histogram of counts.

sections.label: Fit through:
sections.description: The cloud fits the curve to the distribution itself: every populated bin pulls on it, weighted by what it counted, and a bin more than a couple of bins away stops pulling -- so the curve follows the populations and ignores the junk. Reducing each column to one point instead cannot describe a population: a blob reduces to a horizontal streak across its own columns.

sections.label: Scan first
sections.description: Evaluate a coarse grid over the free parameters before the fit and start it at the best point. A least-squares run only goes downhill from where it starts, so a degenerate pair -- a constant that scales the data against a parameter that scales the curve -- otherwise strands it in the first dip. Costs a fixed number of steps.

sections.text: Free parameters are optimised, fixed ones held. Constants and crosslinked parameters start fixed -- free them to fit them.
nDXplorer parameters -- a freed one moves the data, which is re-derived from the equations at every step.

buttons.label: Cancel
buttons.description: Stop the fit after the step it is on.

buttons.label: Fit
buttons.description: Optimise every free parameter against the selected data
